**Barack Hussein Obama** (;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-7) born **Baraka Hussein Obama**,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) 18 June 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10)– 24 November 1982) was a Kenyan senior governmental economist and the father of Barack Obama, the 44th president of the United States. He is a central figure of his son's memoir, _Dreams from My Father_ (1995). Obama married in 1954 and had two children with his first wife, Kezia. He was selected for a special program to attend college in the United States and studied at the University of Hawaii where he met Ann Dunham, whom he married in 1961 following the conception of his son, Barack. Obama and Dunham divorced three years later.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) Obama then went to Harvard University for graduate school, where he earned an MA in economics, and returned to Kenya in 1964. He saw his son Barack once more, when his son was about 10.

In late 1964, Obama married Ruth Beatrice Baker, an American woman he had met in Massachusetts. They had two sons together before separating in 1971 and divorcing in 1973. Obama first worked for an oil company, before beginning work as an economist with the Kenyan Ministry of Transport. He was promoted to senior economic analyst in the Ministry of Finance. He was among a cadre of young Kenyan men who had been educated in the West in a program supported by Tom Mboya. Obama had conflicts with Kenyan presidentJomo Kenyatta, which adversely affected his career. He was fired and blacklisted in Kenya, finding it nearly impossible to get a job. Obama was involved in three serious car accidents during his final years; he died as a result of the last one in 1982.

## Early life
Baraka Hussein Obama was born in 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10) in Rachuonyo District[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) on the shores of Lake Victoria just outside Kendu Bay, Kenya, at the time a colony and protectorate of the British Empire. He was raised in the village of [Nyang'oma Kogelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang'oma_Kogelo "Nyang'oma Kogelo"), Siaya District, Nyanza Province.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ombuor-13) His family were members of the Luo people.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-14) His father was Onyango Obama (c.1895–1979), and his mother was Habiba Akumu Nyanjango (c.1918–2006) of Karabondi, Kenya, Onyango's second wife, with whom, in addition to Baraka, they had two daughters. After his mother left the family in 1945, the three children were raised by Onyango's third wife, Sarah Ogwel of Kogelo.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Powell-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Reitwiesner-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-17)

## Early life
### Religion and education
When Obama was about six years old and attending a Christian missionary school, he converted from Islam to Anglicanism when strongly encouraged by the staff, and changed his name from "Baraka" to "Barack".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) He later became an atheist, contending that religion was mere superstition.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-spiritual_journey-18) While still living near Kendu Bay, Obama attended Gendia Primary School. After his family moved to Siaya District, he transferred to Ng'iya Intermediate School.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) From 1950 to 1953, he studied at Maseno National School, an exclusive Anglican boarding school in Maseno.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-19) The head teacher, B.L. Bowers, described Obama in his records as "very keen, steady, trustworthy and friendly. Concentrates, reliable, and out-going."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008a-20) In 1954 at age 20, Obama married Kezia Aoko[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-21) in a tribal ceremony in Kenya. They had two children, Malik (a.k.a. Roy) and Auma.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Foreman-22)

## College and graduate school
In 1959, the Kenyan Department of Education published Obama's monograph, entitled _Otieno jarieko. Kitabu mar ariyo. 2: Yore mabeyo mag puro puothe._ (English: _Otieno, the wise man. Book 2: Wise ways of farming._)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-24)
Due to his accomplishments, in 1959 Obama received a scholarship in economics through a program organized by the nationalist leader Tom Mboya. The program offered education in the West to outstanding Kenyan students.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Dobbs-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Jacobs_2008-26) Initial financial supporters of the program included Harry Belafonte, Sidney Poitier, Jackie Robinson, and Elizabeth Mooney Kirk, a literacy advocate who provided most of the financial support for Obama's early years in the United States.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-27) Kirk and her literacy associate Helen M. Roberts of Palo Alto raised the money necessary for Obama to travel to the US.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-airlift2009-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-unlikely2009-29)

## College and graduate school
When Obama left for the United States, he left behind his young wife, Kezia, and their baby son Malik. Kezia was pregnant, and their daughter Auma was born while her father was in Hawaii.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Rice-30) At Obama's request, Helen M. Roberts committed to watching over and financially supporting the family that he had left behind, for as long as she remained in Nairobi.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-theotherbarack-31)

## College and graduate school
### University of Hawaii
In 1959, Obama enrolled at the University of Hawaii at Manoa in Honolulu as the university's first African foreign student.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32) He initially lived across the street from the university at the Charles H. Atherton branch of the YMCA at 1810 University Avenue;[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32) public records from 1961 indicate he later had a residence two miles southeast of the university at 625 11th Avenue in the Kaimuki neighborhood.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Hoover-33)

## College and graduate school
### University of Hawaii
In 1960, Obama met Stanley Ann Dunham in a basic Russian language course at the University of Hawaii and they started dating.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32) After becoming pregnant, Dunham dropped out of the University of Hawaii after the fall 1960 semester, while Obama continued his education.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ripley-34) Obama married Dunham in Wailuku on the Hawaiian island of Maui on 2 February 1961, despite parental opposition from both families.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Meacham-36)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ripley-34)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-ForcedOutHarvard-37) He eventually told Dunham about his previous marriage in Kenya, but said he was divorced—which she found out years later was not true.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32)

## College and graduate school
### University of Hawaii
Their son, future US president Barack Hussein Obama II, was born in Honolulu on 4 August 1961 at the former Kapiolani Maternity and Gynecological Hospital (succeeded by the [Kapi'olani Medical Center for Women and Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapi'olani_Medical_Center_for_Women_and_Children "Kapi'olani Medical Center for Women and Children")).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Foreman-22)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) His birth was announced in _The Honolulu Advertiser_ and the _Honolulu Star-Bulletin,_ with his parents' address listed as 6085 Kalanianaole Highway in the Kuliouou neighborhood of Honolulu, seven miles east of the university—the rented home of Dunham's parents, Stanley and Madelyn Dunham.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Hoover-33) Soon after her son's birth, Dunham took the infant with her to Seattle, Washington, where she took classes at the University of Washington from September 1961 to June 1962.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Dougherty-38)

A photograph of Barack Obama's father hangs on the wall of his grandmother Sarah Hussein Obama's house in the Kenyan village of Kogelo. **Ben Curtis/AP Photo******hide caption****

A photograph of Barack Obama's father hangs on the wall of his grandmother Sarah Hussein Obama's house in the Kenyan village of Kogelo.
Ben Curtis/AP Photo
President Obama is the son of a white American mother and a black Kenyan father who met at the University of Hawaii in 1960. The president last saw his father when he was 10, when Obama Sr. made a brief visit to Hawaii from Kenya, where he moved when the future president was just a toddler.
But what was Barack Obama Sr. really like? Biographer Sally H. Jacobs takes an in-depth look at his life — and his legacy — in _The Other Barack: The Bold and Reckless Life of President Obama's Father_.
**The Childhood Of Barack Obama Sr.**
Jacobs tells _Fresh Air_'s Dave Davies that the president's father grew up in an extremely strict household. His father, Onyango, who later changed his name to Hussein, regularly beat his wives and children with a four-pronged whip. He also forced his children to recite long lists of memorized facts before their meals.

###### **_The Other Barack_**
By Sally H. Jacobs
Hardcover, 336 pages
PublicAffairs
List Price: $27.99
Read An Excerpt
"Barack Obama Sr. would have to recite his math tables while standing at the table before he could have any food," Jacobs says. "[Math] was a relatively new concept for Onyango ... and he wanted his son to have this skill."
And when Obama Sr. later went to the village school, he was immediately recognized for his strong math abilities.
"A principal described him to me as the smartest boy in the school," says Jacobs. "He was particularly good at math, even then. That would become his trademark and he would go on to become an economist, but even as a boy he excelled with numbers."
In 1959, Obama Sr. went to study at the University of Hawaii, Manoa, in Honolulu, where he stood out for his fastidious dressing habits, his forays into public speaking and his fabulous dancing skills.
"A woman who had known him in Hawaii told me of how she ... would go down to some of the famous nightclubs with him and start to dance," says Jacobs. "And everybody would watch because he was so beautiful on the floor — and also because he was a black man. Blacks were very few in number in Honolulu and he was the first African student at the University of Hawaii."
**Meeting Stanley Ann Dunham**
A year after Obama Sr. enrolled at the university, he met Stanley Ann Dunham, a 17-year-old from Kansas who was studying Russian.
"Both of them were quite taken with each other," says Jacobs. "This relationship picked up speed pretty quickly. The president describes it in his own memoir _[Dreams from My Father]_ of how drawn they were to each other. [And] in a fairly short time, she becomes pregnant."
Obama Sr. told Dunham that he had divorced Kezia Aoko, his wife in Africa, but that wasn't true. He also did not reveal that he had had two children with Aoko, who, like Obama Sr., was a member of the Luo ethnic group.

###### **_The Other Barack_**
"The thing you have to understand about this is that it was deeply rooted in Luo culture," says Jacobs. "Divorce wasn't common. You could get a divorce but you had to go through a very complex process which involved the couple sitting before a council of elders and then there had to be a return of the dowry."
Later on, Obama Sr. told immigration officials that he thought of himself as divorced in Kenya before he arrived in the United States. Jacobs says that Obama Sr.'s immigration files also show that Obama Sr. and Dunham may have considered putting President Obama up for adoption before he was born.
"I [made a Freedom of Information Act request for] his immigration file because I wanted to confirm the date he arrived in the United States," she says. "In this record, there was an extraordinary memo in which the foreign student adviser at the University of Hawaii has ... realized [Obama Sr.] might have two wives."
In the adviser's memo, she noted that she had asked Obama Sr. about his family situation.
"And he says, 'Don't worry, my wife is pregnant. But she's making arrangements with the Salvation Army to give the baby up,' " says Jacobs. "Now did that really happen? It's not clear. Members of the family on both sides say they've never heard of it ... [But] Obama Sr. had every reason to not want to have that baby in his life at the time. He was, at the time, up for the renewal of his visa. The last thing they were going to look kindly on, if they chose to see it this way, was a bigamist with a mixed-race baby. So Obama Sr. would say that the baby was going to vanish and that baby would be the [future] president of the United States."
**The Birth of Barack Obama Jr.**
Of course, that baby didn't vanish. Shortly after Dunham gave birth to Barack Obama Jr. on Aug. 4, 1961, in Honolulu, she moved with him to Seattle. Obama Sr. stayed in Hawaii, leaving a year later to go to Harvard University for a graduate fellowship in economics. In 1964, Dunham filed for divorce. That same year, Obama Sr. returned to Kenya, which had just obtained its independence the year before, and got a job in management at Shell.

###### **_The Other Barack_**
"Obama [Sr.] makes it less than a year," says Jacobs. "He wasn't fired exactly, but he was not asked back. So he left Shell and gets another potentially terrific job — this one at the Central Bank of Kenya. Again, he runs into trouble within months. He shows up late, he drinks on the job, he has to borrow money and he is asked to leave."
Sally H. Jacobs has been a reporter for more than 30 years, most recently with _The Boston Globe._ She specializes in political reporting and profiles. **Angson C. Dhlakam******hide caption****
Angson C. Dhlakam

Obama Sr. returned to the U.S. in 1971 because his life was falling apart. A third wife was planning to leave him, he had no job and he had suffered massive injuries in a car accident. He spent a short amount of time with his son Barack Jr. in Hawaii and then returned to Kenya, where a second car crash cost him his legs. In 1982, Obama Sr. was in a third car accident and died from his injuries.
All of Obama Sr.'s children, Jacobs says, have had to come to terms with their complicated relationships with their father. Five of his children have written soul-searching memoirs about Obama Sr., including the president's 1995 memoir, _Dreams from My Fathe_ r.
"If Obama the president had had [Barack Obama Sr.] as a father, I think it's fair to say that he wouldn't be the president," she says. "I think he would have had to wrestle with a neglectful father, an insecure person and someone who probably would have prevented him from following the path he close. In _Dreams,_ you feel Obama Jr. struggling with [questions like] 'Who am I? What kind of a man am I? What will I be?' The person he comes out as is clearly very determined and rooted and a responsible person — everything that Obama Sr. was not."

Onyango was Barack’s grandfather, a Kenyan man of the Luo people. Most remember him as an exacting, mean, and difficult man—he carried heavy wooden sticks with which to hit any misbehaving people, adults and children alike. He also kept two machetes, each with its own name, sharpened at all times. Born in 1895, Onyango was the first in the family to adopt Western ways of dressing and working. His father, Obama, disowned him for this. Onyango worked for white colonizers in various capacities, served in the first World War, and eventually learned Western farming techniques, which made him a renowned and admired farmer. He had several wives, including Granny, and was considered both a good husband (in that he stayed married to his wife Helima, who couldn’t have children) and a difficult one (he had impossibly high standards that many wives weren’t able to meet; many returned to their birth families). A man who wanted what he wanted and wouldn’t take no for an answer, Onyango took a woman named Akumu as his second wife, despite the fact that she was already promised to another man. Akumu became the Old Man and Sarah’s biological mother, although after many attempts, she succeeded in running away from her husband. Throughout the Old Man’s childhood, Onyango encouraged his son to be the best in school while ignoring Sarah’s desire to receive an education; he didn’t believe in educating women. He consistently shamed the Old Man for any mistakes, real or imagined, that the Old Man made. This led the Old Man to be secretive and unwilling to ask his father for help. Onyango kept this up to the end and never got to know his son. Auma suspects that the family’s troubles started with Onyango, since Onyango was the only person the Old Man feared.

President Obama is the son of a white American mother and a black Kenyan father who met at the University of Hawaii in 1960. The president last saw his father when he was 10, when Obama Sr. made a brief visit to Hawaii from Kenya, where he moved when the future president was just a toddler.
But what was Barack Obama Sr. really like? Biographer Sally H. Jacobs takes an in-depth look at his life — and his legacy — in _The Other Barack: The Bold and Reckless Life of President Obama's Father_.
**The Childhood Of Barack Obama Sr.**
Jacobs tells _Fresh Air_'s Dave Davies that the president's father grew up in an extremely strict household. His father, Onyango, who later changed his name to Hussein, regularly beat his wives and children with a four-pronged whip. He also forced his children to recite long lists of memorized facts before their meals.

###### **_The Other Barack_**
By Sally H. Jacobs
Hardcover, 336 pages
PublicAffairs
List Price: $27.99
Read An Excerpt
"Barack Obama Sr. would have to recite his math tables while standing at the table before he could have any food," Jacobs says. "[Math] was a relatively new concept for Onyango ... and he wanted his son to have this skill."
And when Obama Sr. later went to the village school, he was immediately recognized for his strong math abilities.
"A principal described him to me as the smartest boy in the school," says Jacobs. "He was particularly good at math, even then. That would become his trademark and he would go on to become an economist, but even as a boy he excelled with numbers."
In 1959, Obama Sr. went to study at the University of Hawaii, Manoa, in Honolulu, where he stood out for his fastidious dressing habits, his forays into public speaking and his fabulous dancing skills.
"A woman who had known him in Hawaii told me of how she ... would go down to some of the famous nightclubs with him and start to dance," says Jacobs. "And everybody would watch because he was so beautiful on the floor — and also because he was a black man. Blacks were very few in number in Honolulu and he was the first African student at the University of Hawaii."
**Meeting Stanley Ann Dunham**
A year after Obama Sr. enrolled at the university, he met Stanley Ann Dunham, a 17-year-old from Kansas who was studying Russian.
"Both of them were quite taken with each other," says Jacobs. "This relationship picked up speed pretty quickly. The president describes it in his own memoir _[Dreams from My Father]_ of how drawn they were to each other. [And] in a fairly short time, she becomes pregnant."
Obama Sr. told Dunham that he had divorced Kezia Aoko, his wife in Africa, but that wasn't true. He also did not reveal that he had had two children with Aoko, who, like Obama Sr., was a member of the Luo ethnic group.
texts.2:
###### **_The Other Barack_**
"The thing you have to understand about this is that it was deeply rooted in Luo culture," says Jacobs. "Divorce wasn't common. You could get a divorce but you had to go through a very complex process which involved the couple sitting before a council of elders and then there had to be a return of the dowry."
Later on, Obama Sr. told immigration officials that he thought of himself as divorced in Kenya before he arrived in the United States. Jacobs says that Obama Sr.'s immigration files also show that Obama Sr. and Dunham may have considered putting President Obama up for adoption before he was born.
"I [made a Freedom of Information Act request for] his immigration file because I wanted to confirm the date he arrived in the United States," she says. "In this record, there was an extraordinary memo in which the foreign student adviser at the University of Hawaii has ... realized [Obama Sr.] might have two wives."
In the adviser's memo, she noted that she had asked Obama Sr. about his family situation.
"And he says, 'Don't worry, my wife is pregnant. But she's making arrangements with the Salvation Army to give the baby up,' " says Jacobs. "Now did that really happen? It's not clear. Members of the family on both sides say they've never heard of it ... [But] Obama Sr. had every reason to not want to have that baby in his life at the time. He was, at the time, up for the renewal of his visa. The last thing they were going to look kindly on, if they chose to see it this way, was a bigamist with a mixed-race baby. So Obama Sr. would say that the baby was going to vanish and that baby would be the [future] president of the United States."
**The Birth of Barack Obama Jr.**
Of course, that baby didn't vanish. Shortly after Dunham gave birth to Barack Obama Jr. on Aug. 4, 1961, in Honolulu, she moved with him to Seattle. Obama Sr. stayed in Hawaii, leaving a year later to go to Harvard University for a graduate fellowship in economics. In 1964, Dunham filed for divorce. That same year, Obama Sr. returned to Kenya, which had just obtained its independence the year before, and got a job in management at Shell.

###### **_The Other Barack_**
"Obama [Sr.] makes it less than a year," says Jacobs. "He wasn't fired exactly, but he was not asked back. So he left Shell and gets another potentially terrific job — this one at the Central Bank of Kenya. Again, he runs into trouble within months. He shows up late, he drinks on the job, he has to borrow money and he is asked to leave."

Obama Sr. returned to the U.S. in 1971 because his life was falling apart. A third wife was planning to leave him, he had no job and he had suffered massive injuries in a car accident. He spent a short amount of time with his son Barack Jr. in Hawaii and then returned to Kenya, where a second car crash cost him his legs. In 1982, Obama Sr. was in a third car accident and died from his injuries.
All of Obama Sr.'s children, Jacobs says, have had to come to terms with their complicated relationships with their father. Five of his children have written soul-searching memoirs about Obama Sr., including the president's 1995 memoir, _Dreams from My Fathe_ r.
"If Obama the president had had [Barack Obama Sr.] as a father, I think it's fair to say that he wouldn't be the president," she says. "I think he would have had to wrestle with a neglectful father, an insecure person and someone who probably would have prevented him from following the path he close. In _Dreams,_ you feel Obama Jr. struggling with [questions like] 'Who am I? What kind of a man am I? What will I be?' The person he comes out as is clearly very determined and rooted and a responsible person — everything that Obama Sr. was not."

texts.1: **Barack Hussein Obama** (;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-7) born **Baraka Hussein Obama**,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) 18 June 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10)– 24 November 1982) was a Kenyan senior governmental economist and the father of Barack Obama, the 44th president of the United States. He is a central figure of his son's memoir, _Dreams from My Father_ (1995). Obama married in 1954 and had two children with his first wife, Kezia. He was selected for a special program to attend college in the United States and studied at the University of Hawaii where he met Ann Dunham, whom he married in 1961 following the conception of his son, Barack. Obama and Dunham divorced three years later.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) Obama then went to Harvard University for graduate school, where he earned an MA in economics, and returned to Kenya in 1964. He saw his son Barack once more, when his son was about 10.
texts.2: In late 1964, Obama married Ruth Beatrice Baker, an American woman he had met in Massachusetts. They had two sons together before separating in 1971 and divorcing in 1973. Obama first worked for an oil company, before beginning work as an economist with the Kenyan Ministry of Transport. He was promoted to senior economic analyst in the Ministry of Finance. He was among a cadre of young Kenyan men who had been educated in the West in a program supported by Tom Mboya. Obama had conflicts with Kenyan presidentJomo Kenyatta, which adversely affected his career. He was fired and blacklisted in Kenya, finding it nearly impossible to get a job. Obama was involved in three serious car accidents during his final years; he died as a result of the last one in 1982.

## Early life
Baraka Hussein Obama was born in 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10) in Rachuonyo District[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) on the shores of Lake Victoria just outside Kendu Bay, Kenya, at the time a colony and protectorate of the British Empire. He was raised in the village of [Nyang'oma Kogelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang'oma_Kogelo "Nyang'oma Kogelo"), Siaya District, Nyanza Province.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ombuor-13) His family were members of the Luo people.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-14) His father was Onyango Obama (c.1895–1979), and his mother was Habiba Akumu Nyanjango (c.1918–2006) of Karabondi, Kenya, Onyango's second wife, with whom, in addition to Baraka, they had two daughters. After his mother left the family in 1945, the three children were raised by Onyango's third wife, Sarah Ogwel of Kogelo.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Powell-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Reitwiesner-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-17)

## Early life
### Religion and education
When Obama was about six years old and attending a Christian missionary school, he converted from Islam to Anglicanism when strongly encouraged by the staff, and changed his name from "Baraka" to "Barack".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) He later became an atheist, contending that religion was mere superstition.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-spiritual_journey-18) While still living near Kendu Bay, Obama attended Gendia Primary School. After his family moved to Siaya District, he transferred to Ng'iya Intermediate School.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) From 1950 to 1953, he studied at Maseno National School, an exclusive Anglican boarding school in Maseno.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-19) The head teacher, B.L. Bowers, described Obama in his records as "very keen, steady, trustworthy and friendly. Concentrates, reliable, and out-going."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008a-20) In 1954 at age 20, Obama married Kezia Aoko[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-21) in a tribal ceremony in Kenya. They had two children, Malik (a.k.a. Roy) and Auma.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Foreman-22)

## College and graduate school
In 1959, the Kenyan Department of Education published Obama's monograph, entitled _Otieno jarieko. Kitabu mar ariyo. 2: Yore mabeyo mag puro puothe._ (English: _Otieno, the wise man. Book 2: Wise ways of farming._)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-24)
Due to his accomplishments, in 1959 Obama received a scholarship in economics through a program organized by the nationalist leader Tom Mboya. The program offered education in the West to outstanding Kenyan students.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Dobbs-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Jacobs_2008-26) Initial financial supporters of the program included Harry Belafonte, Sidney Poitier, Jackie Robinson, and Elizabeth Mooney Kirk, a literacy advocate who provided most of the financial support for Obama's early years in the United States.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-27) Kirk and her literacy associate Helen M. Roberts of Palo Alto raised the money necessary for Obama to travel to the US.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-airlift2009-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-unlikely2009-29)

When Obama left for the United States, he left behind his young wife, Kezia, and their baby son Malik. Kezia was pregnant, and their daughter Auma was born while her father was in Hawaii.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Rice-30) At Obama's request, Helen M. ## College and graduate school
### University of Hawaii
In 1959, Obama enrolled at the University of Hawaii at Manoa in Honolulu as the university's first African foreign student.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32) He initially lived across the street from the university at the Charles H. Atherton branch of the YMCA at 1810 University Avenue;[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32) public records from 1961 indicate he later had a residence two miles southeast of the university at 625 11th Avenue in the Kaimuki neighborhood.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Hoover-33)

## College and graduate school
### University of Hawaii
In 1960, Obama met Stanley Ann Dunham in a basic Russian language course at the University of Hawaii and they started dating.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32) After becoming pregnant, Dunham dropped out of the University of Hawaii after the fall 1960 semester, while Obama continued his education.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ripley-34) Obama married Dunham in Wailuku on the Hawaiian island of Maui on 2 February 1961, despite parental opposition from both families.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Meacham-36)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ripley-34)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-ForcedOutHarvard-37) He eventually told Dunham about his previous marriage in Kenya, but said he was divorced—which she found out years later was not true.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32)

## College and graduate school
### University of Hawaii
Their son, future US president Barack Hussein Obama II, was born in Honolulu on 4 August 1961 at the former Kapiolani Maternity and Gynecological Hospital (succeeded by the [Kapi'olani Medical Center for Women and Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapi'olani_Medical_Center_for_Women_and_Children "Kapi'olani Medical Center for Women and Children")).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Foreman-22)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) His birth was announced in _The Honolulu Advertiser_ and the _Honolulu Star-Bulletin,_ with his parents' address listed as 6085 Kalanianaole Highway in the Kuliouou neighborhood of Honolulu, seven miles east of the university—the rented home of Dunham's parents, Stanley and Madelyn Dunham.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Hoover-33) Soon after her son's birth, Dunham took the infant with her to Seattle, Washington, where she took classes at the University of Washington from September 1961 to June 1962.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Dougherty-38)

texts.0: Onyango was Barack’s grandfather, a Kenyan man of the Luo people. Most remember him as an exacting, mean, and difficult man—he carried heavy wooden sticks with which to hit any misbehaving people, adults and children alike. He also kept two machetes, each with its own name, sharpened at all times. Born in 1895, Onyango was the first in the family to adopt Western ways of dressing and working. His father, Obama, disowned him for this. Onyango worked for white colonizers in various capacities, served in the first World War, and eventually learned Western farming techniques, which made him a renowned and admired farmer. He had several wives, including Granny, and was considered both a good husband (in that he stayed married to his wife Helima, who couldn’t have children) and a difficult one (he had impossibly high standards that many wives weren’t able to meet; many returned to their birth families). A man who wanted what he wanted and wouldn’t take no for an answer, Onyango took a woman named Akumu as his second wife, despite the fact that she was already promised to another man. Akumu became the Old Man and Sarah’s biological mother, although after many attempts, she succeeded in running away from her husband. Throughout the Old Man’s childhood, Onyango encouraged his son to be the best in school while ignoring Sarah’s desire to receive an education; he didn’t believe in educating women. He consistently shamed the Old Man for any mistakes, real or imagined, that the Old Man made. This led the Old Man to be secretive and unwilling to ask his father for help. Onyango kept this up to the end and never got to know his son. Auma suspects that the family’s troubles started with Onyango, since Onyango was the only person the Old Man feared.

President Obama is the son of a white American mother and a black Kenyan father who met at the University of Hawaii in 1960. The president last saw his father when he was 10, when Obama Sr. made a brief visit to Hawaii from Kenya, where he moved when the future president was just a toddler.
But what was Barack Obama Sr. really like? Biographer Sally H. Jacobs takes an in-depth look at his life — and his legacy — in _The Other Barack: The Bold and Reckless Life of President Obama's Father_.
**The Childhood Of Barack Obama Sr.**
Jacobs tells _Fresh Air_'s Dave Davies that the president's father grew up in an extremely strict household. His father, Onyango, who later changed his name to Hussein, regularly beat his wives and children with a four-pronged whip. He also forced his children to recite long lists of memorized facts before their meals.

"Barack Obama Sr. would have to recite his math tables while standing at the table before he could have any food," Jacobs says. "[Math] was a relatively new concept for Onyango ... and he wanted his son to have this skill."
And when Obama Sr. later went to the village school, he was immediately recognized for his strong math abilities.
"A principal described him to me as the smartest boy in the school," says Jacobs. "He was particularly good at math, even then. That would become his trademark and he would go on to become an economist, but even as a boy he excelled with numbers."
In 1959, Obama Sr. went to study at the University of Hawaii, Manoa, in Honolulu, where he stood out for his fastidious dressing habits, his forays into public speaking and his fabulous dancing skills.
"A woman who had known him in Hawaii told me of how she ... would go down to some of the famous nightclubs with him and start to dance," says Jacobs. "And everybody would watch because he was so beautiful on the floor — and also because he was a black man. Blacks were very few in number in Honolulu and he was the first African student at the University of Hawaii."
**Meeting Stanley Ann Dunham**
A year after Obama Sr. enrolled at the university, he met Stanley Ann Dunham, a 17-year-old from Kansas who was studying Russian.
"Both of them were quite taken with each other," says Jacobs. "This relationship picked up speed pretty quickly. The president describes it in his own memoir _[Dreams from My Father]_ of how drawn they were to each other. [And] in a fairly short time, she becomes pregnant."
Obama Sr. told Dunham that he had divorced Kezia Aoko, his wife in Africa, but that wasn't true. He also did not reveal that he had had two children with Aoko, who, like Obama Sr., was a member of the Luo ethnic group.

###### **_The Other Barack_**
"The thing you have to understand about this is that it was deeply rooted in Luo culture," says Jacobs. "Divorce wasn't common. You could get a divorce but you had to go through a very complex process which involved the couple sitting before a council of elders and then there had to be a return of the dowry."
Later on, Obama Sr. told immigration officials that he thought of himself as divorced in Kenya before he arrived in the United States. Jacobs says that Obama Sr.'s immigration files also show that Obama Sr. and Dunham may have considered putting President Obama up for adoption before he was born.
"I [made a Freedom of Information Act request for] his immigration file because I wanted to confirm the date he arrived in the United States," she says. "In this record, there was an extraordinary memo in which the foreign student adviser at the University of Hawaii has ... realized [Obama Sr.] might have two wives."
In the adviser's memo, she noted that she had asked Obama Sr. about his family situation.
"And he says, 'Don't worry, my wife is pregnant. But she's making arrangements with the Salvation Army to give the baby up,' " says Jacobs. "Now did that really happen? It's not clear. Members of the family on both sides say they've never heard of it ... [But] Obama Sr. had every reason to not want to have that baby in his life at the time. He was, at the time, up for the renewal of his visa. The last thing they were going to look kindly on, if they chose to see it this way, was a bigamist with a mixed-race baby. So Obama Sr. would say that the baby was going to vanish and that baby would be the [future] president of the United States."
**The Birth of Barack Obama Jr.**
Of course, that baby didn't vanish. Shortly after Dunham gave birth to Barack Obama Jr. on Aug. 4, 1961, in Honolulu, she moved with him to Seattle. Obama Sr. stayed in Hawaii, leaving a year later to go to Harvard University for a graduate fellowship in economics. In 1964, Dunham filed for divorce. That same year, Obama Sr. returned to Kenya, which had just obtained its independence the year before, and got a job in management at Shell.

**Barack Hussein Obama** (;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-7) born **Baraka Hussein Obama**,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) 18 June 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10)– 24 November 1982) was a Kenyan senior governmental economist and the father of Barack Obama, the 44th president of the United States. He is a central figure of his son's memoir, _Dreams from My Father_ (1995). Obama married in 1954 and had two children with his first wife, Kezia. He was selected for a special program to attend college in the United States and studied at the University of Hawaii where he met Ann Dunham, whom he married in 1961 following the conception of his son, Barack. Obama and Dunham divorced three years later.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) Obama then went to Harvard University for graduate school, where he earned an MA in economics, and returned to Kenya in 1964. He saw his son Barack once more, when his son was about 10.

In late 1964, Obama married Ruth Beatrice Baker, an American woman he had met in Massachusetts. They had two sons together before separating in 1971 and divorcing in 1973. Obama first worked for an oil company, before beginning work as an economist with the Kenyan Ministry of Transport. He was promoted to senior economic analyst in the Ministry of Finance. He was among a cadre of young Kenyan men who had been educated in the West in a program supported by Tom Mboya. Obama had conflicts with Kenyan presidentJomo Kenyatta, which adversely affected his career. He was fired and blacklisted in Kenya, finding it nearly impossible to get a job. Obama was involved in three serious car accidents during his final years; he died as a result of the last one in 1982.

## Early life
Baraka Hussein Obama was born in 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10) in Rachuonyo District[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) on the shores of Lake Victoria just outside Kendu Bay, Kenya, at the time a colony and protectorate of the British Empire. He was raised in the village of [Nyang'oma Kogelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang'oma_Kogelo "Nyang'oma Kogelo"), Siaya District, Nyanza Province.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ombuor-13) His family were members of the Luo people.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-14) His father was Onyango Obama (c.1895–1979), and his mother was Habiba Akumu Nyanjango (c.1918–2006) of Karabondi, Kenya, Onyango's second wife, with whom, in addition to Baraka, they had two daughters. After his mother left the family in 1945, the three children were raised by Onyango's third wife, Sarah Ogwel of Kogelo.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Powell-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Reitwiesner-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-17)

## Early life
### Religion and education
When Obama was about six years old and attending a Christian missionary school, he converted from Islam to Anglicanism when strongly encouraged by the staff, and changed his name from "Baraka" to "Barack".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) He later became an atheist, contending that religion was mere superstition.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-spiritual_journey-18) While still living near Kendu Bay, Obama attended Gendia Primary School. After his family moved to Siaya District, he transferred to Ng'iya Intermediate School.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) From 1950 to 1953, he studied at Maseno National School, an exclusive Anglican boarding school in Maseno.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-19) The head teacher, B.L. Bowers, described Obama in his records as "very keen, steady, trustworthy and friendly. Concentrates, reliable, and out-going."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008a-20) In 1954 at age 20, Obama married Kezia Aoko[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-21) in a tribal ceremony in Kenya. They had two children, Malik (a.k.a. Roy) and Auma.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Foreman-22)

## College and graduate school
In 1959, the Kenyan Department of Education published Obama's monograph, entitled _Otieno jarieko. Kitabu mar ariyo. 2: Yore mabeyo mag puro puothe._ (English: _Otieno, the wise man. Book 2: Wise ways of farming._)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-24)
Due to his accomplishments, in 1959 Obama received a scholarship in economics through a program organized by the nationalist leader Tom Mboya. The program offered education in the West to outstanding Kenyan students.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Dobbs-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Jacobs_2008-26) Initial financial supporters of the program included Harry Belafonte, Sidney Poitier, Jackie Robinson, and Elizabeth Mooney Kirk, a literacy advocate who provided most of the financial support for Obama's early years in the United States.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-27) Kirk and her literacy associate Helen M. Roberts of Palo Alto raised the money necessary for Obama to travel to the US.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-airlift2009-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-unlikely2009-29)

## College and graduate school
When Obama left for the United States, he left behind his young wife, Kezia, and their baby son Malik. Kezia was pregnant, and their daughter Auma was born while her father was in Hawaii.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Rice-30) At Obama's request, Helen M. Roberts committed to watching over and financially supporting the family that he had left behind, for as long as she remained in Nairobi.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-theotherbarack-31)

## College and graduate school
### University of Hawaii
In 1959, Obama enrolled at the University of Hawaii at Manoa in Honolulu as the university's first African foreign student.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32) He initially lived across the street from the university at the Charles H. Atherton branch of the YMCA at 1810 University Avenue;[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32) public records from 1961 indicate he later had a residence two miles southeast of the university at 625 11th Avenue in the Kaimuki neighborhood.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Hoover-33)

## College and graduate school
### University of Hawaii
In 1960, Obama met Stanley Ann Dunham in a basic Russian language course at the University of Hawaii and they started dating.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32) After becoming pregnant, Dunham dropped out of the University of Hawaii after the fall 1960 semester, while Obama continued his education.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ripley-34) Obama married Dunham in Wailuku on the Hawaiian island of Maui on 2 February 1961, despite parental opposition from both families.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Meacham-36)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ripley-34)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-ForcedOutHarvard-37) He eventually told Dunham about his previous marriage in Kenya, but said he was divorced—which she found out years later was not true.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32)

## College and graduate school
### University of Hawaii
Their son, future US president Barack Hussein Obama II, was born in Honolulu on 4 August 1961 at the former Kapiolani Maternity and Gynecological Hospital (succeeded by the [Kapi'olani Medical Center for Women and Children](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapi'olani_Medical_Center_for_Women_and_Children "Kapi'olani Medical Center for Women and Children")).[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss-32)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Foreman-22)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) His birth was announced in _The Honolulu Advertiser_ and the _Honolulu Star-Bulletin,_ with his parents' address listed as 6085 Kalanianaole Highway in the Kuliouou neighborhood of Honolulu, seven miles east of the university—the rented home of Dunham's parents, Stanley and Madelyn Dunham.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Hoover-33) Soon after her son's birth, Dunham took the infant with her to Seattle, Washington, where she took classes at the University of Washington from September 1961 to June 1962.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Dougherty-38)

He was among a cadre of young Kenyan men who had been educated in the West in a program supported by Tom Mboya. Obama had conflicts with Kenyan presidentJomo Kenyatta, which adversely affected his career. He was fired and blacklisted in Kenya, finding it nearly impossible to get a job. Obama was involved in three serious car accidents during his final years; he died as a result of the last one in 1982.

## Early life
Baraka Hussein Obama was born in 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10) in Rachuonyo District[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) on the shores of Lake Victoria just outside Kendu Bay, Kenya, at the time a colony and protectorate of the British Empire. He was raised in the village of [Nyang'oma Kogelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyang'oma_Kogelo "Nyang'oma Kogelo"), Siaya District, Nyanza Province.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Ombuor-13) His family were members of the Luo people.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-14) His father was Onyango Obama (c.1895–1979), and his mother was Habiba Akumu Nyanjango (c.1918–2006) of Karabondi, Kenya, Onyango's second wife, with whom, in addition to Baraka, they had two daughters. After his mother left the family in 1945, the three children were raised by Onyango's third wife, Sarah Ogwel of Kogelo.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Powell-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Reitwiesner-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-17)

## Early life
### Religion and education
When Obama was about six years old and attending a Christian missionary school, he converted from Islam to Anglicanism when strongly encouraged by the staff, and changed his name from "Baraka" to "Barack".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) He later became an atheist, contending that religion was mere superstition.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-spiritual_journey-18) While still living near Kendu Bay, Obama attended Gendia Primary School. After his family moved to Siaya District, he transferred to Ng'iya Intermediate School.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008b-12) From 1950 to 1953, he studied at Maseno National School, an exclusive Anglican boarding school in Maseno.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-19) The head teacher, B.L. Bowers, described Obama in his records as "very keen, steady, trustworthy and friendly. Concentrates, reliable, and out-going."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Oywa_2008a-20) In 1954 at age 20, Obama married Kezia Aoko[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-21) in a tribal ceremony in Kenya. They had two children, Malik (a.k.a. Roy) and Auma.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Foreman-22)

A photograph of Barack Obama's father hangs on the wall of his grandmother Sarah Hussein Obama's house in the Kenyan village of Kogelo. **Ben Curtis/AP Photo******hide caption****
Ben Curtis/AP Photo
A photograph of Barack Obama's father hangs on the wall of his grandmother Sarah Hussein Obama's house in the Kenyan village of Kogelo.
Ben Curtis/AP Photo
President Obama is the son of a white American mother and a black Kenyan father who met at the University of Hawaii in 1960. The president last saw his father when he was 10, when Obama Sr. made a brief visit to Hawaii from Kenya, where he moved when the future president was just a toddler.
But what was Barack Obama Sr. really like? Biographer Sally H. Jacobs takes an in-depth look at his life — and his legacy — in _The Other Barack: The Bold and Reckless Life of President Obama's Father_.
**The Childhood Of Barack Obama Sr.**
Jacobs tells _Fresh Air_'s Dave Davies that the president's father grew up in an extremely strict household. His father, Onyango, who later changed his name to Hussein, regularly beat his wives and children with a four-pronged whip. He also forced his children to recite long lists of memorized facts before their meals.

###### **_The Other Barack_**
By Sally H. Jacobs
Hardcover, 336 pages
PublicAffairs
List Price: $27.99
Read An Excerpt
"Barack Obama Sr. would have to recite his math tables while standing at the table before he could have any food," Jacobs says. "[Math] was a relatively new concept for Onyango ... and he wanted his son to have this skill."
And when Obama Sr. later went to the village school, he was immediately recognized for his strong math abilities.
"A principal described him to me as the smartest boy in the school," says Jacobs. "He was particularly good at math, even then. That would become his trademark and he would go on to become an economist, but even as a boy he excelled with numbers."
In 1959, Obama Sr. went to study at the University of Hawaii, Manoa, in Honolulu, where he stood out for his fastidious dressing habits, his forays into public speaking and his fabulous dancing skills.
"A woman who had known him in Hawaii told me of how she ... would go down to some of the famous nightclubs with him and start to dance," says Jacobs. "And everybody would watch because he was so beautiful on the floor — and also because he was a black man. Blacks were very few in number in Honolulu and he was the first African student at the University of Hawaii."
**Meeting Stanley Ann Dunham**
A year after Obama Sr. enrolled at the university, he met Stanley Ann Dunham, a 17-year-old from Kansas who was studying Russian.
"Both of them were quite taken with each other," says Jacobs. "This relationship picked up speed pretty quickly. The president describes it in his own memoir _[Dreams from My Father]_ of how drawn they were to each other. [And] in a fairly short time, she becomes pregnant."
Obama Sr. told Dunham that he had divorced Kezia Aoko, his wife in Africa, but that wasn't true. He also did not reveal that he had had two children with Aoko, who, like Obama Sr., was a member of the Luo ethnic group.

###### **_The Other Barack_**
"The thing you have to understand about this is that it was deeply rooted in Luo culture," says Jacobs. "Divorce wasn't common. You could get a divorce but you had to go through a very complex process which involved the couple sitting before a council of elders and then there had to be a return of the dowry."
Later on, Obama Sr. told immigration officials that he thought of himself as divorced in Kenya before he arrived in the United States. Jacobs says that Obama Sr.'s immigration files also show that Obama Sr. and Dunham may have considered putting President Obama up for adoption before he was born.
"I [made a Freedom of Information Act request for] his immigration file because I wanted to confirm the date he arrived in the United States," she says. "In this record, there was an extraordinary memo in which the foreign student adviser at the University of Hawaii has ... realized [Obama Sr.] might have two wives."
In the adviser's memo, she noted that she had asked Obama Sr. about his family situation.
"And he says, 'Don't worry, my wife is pregnant. But she's making arrangements with the Salvation Army to give the baby up,' " says Jacobs. "Now did that really happen? It's not clear. Members of the family on both sides say they've never heard of it ... [But] Obama Sr. had every reason to not want to have that baby in his life at the time. He was, at the time, up for the renewal of his visa. The last thing they were going to look kindly on, if they chose to see it this way, was a bigamist with a mixed-race baby. So Obama Sr. would say that the baby was going to vanish and that baby would be the [future] president of the United States."
**The Birth of Barack Obama Jr.**
Of course, that baby didn't vanish. Shortly after Dunham gave birth to Barack Obama Jr. on Aug. 4, 1961, in Honolulu, she moved with him to Seattle. Obama Sr. stayed in Hawaii, leaving a year later to go to Harvard University for a graduate fellowship in economics. In 1964, Dunham filed for divorce. That same year, Obama Sr. returned to Kenya, which had just obtained its independence the year before, and got a job in management at Shell.

###### **_The Other Barack_**
"Obama [Sr.] makes it less than a year," says Jacobs. "He wasn't fired exactly, but he was not asked back. So he left Shell and gets another potentially terrific job — this one at the Central Bank of Kenya. Again, he runs into trouble within months. He shows up late, he drinks on the job, he has to borrow money and he is asked to leave."
Sally H. Jacobs has been a reporter for more than 30 years, most recently with _The Boston Globe._ She specializes in political reporting and profiles. **Angson C. Dhlakam******hide caption****
Angson C. Dhlakam
Sally H. Jacobs has been a reporter for more than 30 years, most recently with _The Boston Globe._ She specializes in political reporting and profiles.
Angson C. Dhlakam
Obama Sr. returned to the U.S. in 1971 because his life was falling apart. A third wife was planning to leave him, he had no job and he had suffered massive injuries in a car accident. He spent a short amount of time with his son Barack Jr. in Hawaii and then returned to Kenya, where a second car crash cost him his legs. In 1982, Obama Sr. was in a third car accident and died from his injuries.
All of Obama Sr.'s children, Jacobs says, have had to come to terms with their complicated relationships with their father. Five of his children have written soul-searching memoirs about Obama Sr., including the president's 1995 memoir, _Dreams from My Fathe_ r.
"If Obama the president had had [Barack Obama Sr.] as a father, I think it's fair to say that he wouldn't be the president," she says. "I think he would have had to wrestle with a neglectful father, an insecure person and someone who probably would have prevented him from following the path he close. In _Dreams,_ you feel Obama Jr. struggling with [questions like] 'Who am I? What kind of a man am I? What will I be?' The person he comes out as is clearly very determined and rooted and a responsible person — everything that Obama Sr. was not."

###### The Other Barack
The Bold and Reckless Life of President Obama's Father
By Sally Jacobs

# Trench Lens - "Long before Barack Obama ever set foot in... | Facebook
## Trench Lens's Post
"Long before Barack Obama ever set foot in Downing Street as a guest of honor, his family's history with Britain was already written in pain, and it is one of the most quietly staggering facts about his heritage that most people never learn. His paternal grandfather, Hussein Onyango Obama, was a cook working for British officers in colonial Kenya, and during the brutal crackdown on the Mau Mau uprising he was detained and, according to Obama's own account in his memoir, subjected to torture at the hands of British colonial forces who suspected him of aiding the rebellion. Think about that for a second. Decades before his grandson would stand in Westminster Hall as President of the United States, receiving applause reserved for popes and queens, his own flesh and blood was a prisoner of the empire that grandson would later call one of America's closest allies. Obama wrote candidly about this legacy, describing how it shaped his understanding of colonialism, power, and the complicated inheritance of history that every leader carries whether the cameras see it or not. It is why some historians and commentators noted, well before his first term even began, that Obama arrived in the Oval Office without the instinctive nostalgic warmth toward Britain that so many of his predecessors carried, men who had fought alongside British troops or grown up steeped in Anglophile tradition. His was a relationship built not on inherited sentiment but on something harder and more honest, a recognition of shared interest forged in spite of a painful family past rather than because of an easy one. And yet what makes this story so moving is not the wound itself but what came after, a grandson of a colonial prisoner standing shoulder to shoulder with a British prime minister, praised by a queen as a valued friend, invited to sleep beneath the roof of Buckingham Palace itself. That arc, from a jail cell in Kenya to the state rooms of the palace, is the kind of history that novels are built on, except it is completely real, documented, and largely forgotten in the noise of modern headlines. It forces you to sit with a bigger truth, that nations do not owe each other comfort, they owe each other honesty, and the strongest alliances are often the ones built by people who never forgot where the scars came from.

# Trench Lens - "Long before Barack Obama ever set foot in... | Facebook
## Trench Lens's Post
Obama never hid this history to make anyone comfortable, and that refusal to sanitize his own story is exactly why it still hits so hard today, reminding us that reconciliation is not about forgetting, it is about remembering fully and choosing connection anyway, a lesson that feels more urgent with every passing year of division we see in the world around us."

In 1959, Obama Sr. went to study at the University of Hawaii, Manoa, in Honolulu, where he stood out for his fastidious dressing habits, his forays into public speaking and his fabulous dancing skills.
"A woman who had known him in Hawaii told me of how she ... would go down to some of the famous nightclubs with him and start to dance," says Jacobs. "And everybody would watch because he was so beautiful on the floor — and also because he was a black man. Blacks were very few in number in Honolulu and he was the first African student at the University of Hawaii."

A year after Obama Sr. enrolled at the university, he met Stanley Ann Dunham, a 17-year-old from Kansas who was studying Russian.
"Both of them were quite taken with each other," says Jacobs. "This relationship picked up speed pretty quickly. The president describes it in his own memoir _[Dreams from My Father]_ of how drawn they were to each other. [And] in a fairly short time, she becomes pregnant."
Obama Sr. told Dunham that he had divorced Kezia Aoko, his wife in Africa, but that wasn't true. He also did not reveal that he had had two children with Aoko, who, like Obama Sr., was a member of the Luo ethnic group.

###### **_The Other Barack_**
"The thing you have to understand about this is that it was deeply rooted in Luo culture," says Jacobs. "Divorce wasn't common. You could get a divorce but you had to go through a very complex process which involved the couple sitting before a council of elders and then there had to be a return of the dowry."
Later on, Obama Sr. told immigration officials that he thought of himself as divorced in Kenya before he arrived in the United States. Jacobs says that Obama Sr.'s immigration files also show that Obama Sr. and Dunham may have considered putting President Obama up for adoption before he was born.
"I [made a Freedom of Information Act request for] his immigration file because I wanted to confirm the date he arrived in the United States," she says. "In this record, there was an extraordinary memo in which the foreign student adviser at the University of Hawaii has ... realized [Obama Sr.] might have two wives."
In the adviser's memo, she noted that she had asked Obama Sr. about his family situation.
"And he says, 'Don't worry, my wife is pregnant. But she's making arrangements with the Salvation Army to give the baby up,' " says Jacobs. "Now did that really happen? It's not clear. Members of the family on both sides say they've never heard of it ... [But] Obama Sr. had every reason to not want to have that baby in his life at the time. He was, at the time, up for the renewal of his visa. The last thing they were going to look kindly on, if they chose to see it this way, was a bigamist with a mixed-race baby. So Obama Sr. would say that the baby was going to vanish and that baby would be the [future] president of the United States."
**The Birth of Barack Obama Jr.**
Of course, that baby didn't vanish. Shortly after Dunham gave birth to Barack Obama Jr. on Aug. 4, 1961, in Honolulu, she moved with him to Seattle. Obama Sr. stayed in Hawaii, leaving a year later to go to Harvard University for a graduate fellowship in economics. In 1964, Dunham filed for divorce. That same year, Obama Sr. returned to Kenya, which had just obtained its independence the year before, and got a job in management at Shell.

"Obama [Sr.] makes it less than a year," says Jacobs. "He wasn't fired exactly, but he was not asked back. So he left Shell and gets another potentially terrific job — this one at the Central Bank of Kenya. Again, he runs into trouble within months. He shows up late, he drinks on the job, he has to borrow money and he is asked to leave."

texts.1: **Barack Hussein Obama** (;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-7) born **Baraka Hussein Obama**,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) 18 June 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10)– 24 November 1982) was a Kenyan senior governmental economist and the father of Barack Obama, the 44th president of the United States. He is a central figure of his son's memoir, _Dreams from My Father_ (1995). Obama married in 1954 and had two children with his first wife, Kezia. He was selected for a special program to attend college in the United States and studied at the University of Hawaii where he met Ann Dunham, whom he married in 1961 following the conception of his son, Barack. Obama and Dunham divorced three years later.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) Obama then went to Harvard University for graduate school, where he earned an MA in economics, and returned to Kenya in 1964. He saw his son Barack once more, when his son was about 10.
texts.2: In late 1964, Obama married Ruth Beatrice Baker, an American woman he had met in Massachusetts. They had two sons together before separating in 1971 and divorcing in 1973. Obama first worked for an oil company, before beginning work as an economist with the Kenyan Ministry of Transport. He was promoted to senior economic analyst in the Ministry of Finance. He was among a cadre of young Kenyan men who had been educated in the West in a program supported by Tom Mboya. Obama had conflicts with Kenyan presidentJomo Kenyatta, which adversely affected his career. He was fired and blacklisted in Kenya, finding it nearly impossible to get a job. "Long before Barack Obama ever set foot in Downing Street as a guest of honor, his family's history with Britain was already written in pain, and it is one of the most quietly staggering facts about his heritage that most people never learn. His paternal grandfather, Hussein Onyango Obama, was a cook working for British officers in colonial Kenya, and during the brutal crackdown on the Mau Mau uprising he was detained and, according to Obama's own account in his memoir, subjected to torture at the hands of British colonial forces who suspected him of aiding the rebellion. Think about that for a second. Decades before his grandson would stand in Westminster Hall as President of the United States, receiving applause reserved for popes and queens, his own flesh and blood was a prisoner of the empire that grandson would later call one of America's closest allies. Obama wrote candidly about this legacy, describing how it shaped his understanding of colonialism, power, and the complicated inheritance of history that every leader carries whether the cameras see it or not. It is why some historians and commentators noted, well before his first term even began, that Obama arrived in the Oval Office without the instinctive nostalgic warmth toward Britain that so many of his predecessors carried, men who had fought alongside British troops or grown up steeped in Anglophile tradition. His was a relationship built not on inherited sentiment but on something harder and more honest, a recognition of shared interest forged in spite of a painful family past rather than because of an easy one. And yet what makes this story so moving is not the wound itself but what came after, a grandson of a colonial prisoner standing shoulder to shoulder with a British prime minister, praised by a queen as a valued friend, invited to sleep beneath the roof of Buckingham Palace itself. That arc, from a jail cell in Kenya to the state rooms of the palace, is the kind of history that novels are built on, except it is completely real, documented, and largely forgotten in the noise of modern headlines. It forces you to sit with a bigger truth, that nations do not owe each other comfort, they owe each other honesty, and the strongest alliances are often the ones built by people who never forgot where the scars came from.

**Barack Hussein Obama** (;[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-7) born **Baraka Hussein Obama**,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-books.google-8) 18 June 1934[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Maraniss_p._65-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Liberties_p._202-10)– 24 November 1982) was a Kenyan senior governmental economist and the father of Barack Obama, the 44th president of the United States. He is a central figure of his son's memoir, _Dreams from My Father_ (1995). Obama married in 1954 and had two children with his first wife, Kezia. He was selected for a special program to attend college in the United States and studied at the University of Hawaii where he met Ann Dunham, whom he married in 1961 following the conception of his son, Barack. Obama and Dunham divorced three years later.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Cejka-11) Obama then went to Harvard University for graduate school, where he earned an MA in economics, and returned to Kenya in 1964. He saw his son Barack once more, when his son was about 10.

In late 1964, Obama married Ruth Beatrice Baker, an American woman he had met in Massachusetts. They had two sons together before separating in 1971 and divorcing in 1973. Obama first worked for an oil company, before beginning work as an economist with the Kenyan Ministry of Transport. He was promoted to senior economic analyst in the Ministry of Finance. He was among a cadre of young Kenyan men who had been educated in the West in a program supported by Tom Mboya. Obama had conflicts with Kenyan presidentJomo Kenyatta, which adversely affected his career. He was fired and blacklisted in Kenya, finding it nearly impossible to get a job. Obama was involved in three serious car accidents during his final years; he died as a result of the last one in 1982.

After his mother left the family in 1945, the three children were raised by Onyango's third wife, Sarah Ogwel of Kogelo.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Powell-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-Reitwiesner-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Sr.#cite_note-17)
